prompt.en: You hear a distress station break into a routine repeater contact, but you cannot provide direct help yourself. Which combined response fits the lesson?

text.en: Acknowledge the station, collect location and needed assistance, contact authorities if needed, and keep watch.
Leave the frequency at once because a station that cannot help directly has no further role.
Finish the routine contact first, then check whether the distress station is still calling.
Log the call and stay silent permanently so authorities will discover the traffic another way.

explanation.en: The response combines immediate distress handling with the fallback duty when you cannot assist directly: get actionable details, notify the right help, and remain available.

prompt.en: A shelter station owns a battery box but has never powered the radio from it. Which two-step preparation best supports outage communication?

text.en: Charge the battery and test the radio, cable, and connectors on receive and transmit before the outage.
Store the battery uncharged and plan to find the correct cable after commercial power fails.
Test only the radio display, because connector heating cannot affect an emergency contact.
Wait for a real emergency to test the setup so battery capacity is not used during practice.

explanation.en: Backup power is useful only if it is charged and the whole path to the radio works under load. A stored battery by itself is not a tested station.

prompt.en: A net has a routine supply request, an isolated operator needing help with no immediate risk to life, and a station reporting life-threatening injury. Which ranking fits the lesson?

text.en: Handle the life-threatening distress first, then the urgent help request, while routine traffic waits.
Handle routine supply traffic first if it was listed on the net agenda before the emergency.
Treat every help request as distress even when the message says there is no immediate risk to life.
Delay the life-threatening traffic until the isolated operator confirms whether the request is routine.

explanation.en: Life-threatening distress takes priority. A serious request without immediate risk to life is urgent in this lesson, and routine traffic waits for both.
